body.label: Assumption A1
body.caption: Sub-Gaussian noise with variance proxy σ²

statement.text: The noise variables \varepsilon_1, \dots, \varepsilon_n are independent, centred and sub-Gaussian with variance proxy \sigma^2.
For a penalty \mathrm{pen}(\theta) \ge 0, let \hat\theta \in \arg\min_\theta \{ R_n(\theta) + \mathrm{pen}(\theta) \} denote a penalised empirical risk minimiser.
For independent centred variables with |X_i| <= b and total variance v, the sum exceeds t with probability at most exp(-t^2 / (2 (v + b t / 3))).

body.label: Lemma 3.1
body.caption: Uniform concentration of the empirical process

statement.text: For every \delta \in (0,1), with probability at least 1 - \delta, \sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} |P_n f - P f| \le C \sigma \sqrt{(d + \log(1/\delta))/n}.

body.label: Lemma 3.2
body.caption: Bias bound under the design condition

statement.text: If n \ge d \log d, the bias of \hat\theta satisfies \|\mathbb{E}\hat\theta - \theta^*\|_2 \le C \sqrt{d/n}.

body.label: Proposition 3.3
body.caption: Oracle inequality for the penalised estimator

statement.text: With probability at least 1 - \delta, R(\hat\theta) - R(\theta^*) \le 2 \, \mathrm{pen}(\theta^*) + C \sigma^2 (d + \log(1/\delta)) / n.

body.label: Theorem 4.1
body.caption: Minimax-optimal rate for the penalised estimator

statement.text: Under Assumption A1 and the design condition n \ge d \log d, the penalised estimator satisfies \mathbb{E}\|\hat\theta - \theta^*\|_2^2 \le C \sigma^2 d / n, and this rate is minimax optimal.

body.label: Theorem 5.1
body.caption: Standalone result without recorded premises

statement.text: The estimator remains consistent when the penalty is replaced by its data-driven counterpart.

body.rationale: Both regimes are half-open intervals whose union is [d log d, infinity).

body.excerpt:
Assumption A1 (noise). The errors ε_1, …, ε_n are independent, centred and sub-Gaussian with
variance proxy σ^2, i.e. E exp(λ ε_i) ≤ exp(λ^2 σ^2 / 2) for every λ ∈ R.

Definition 2.1. For a penalty pen(θ) ≥ 0 let θ̂ ∈ argmin_θ { R_n(θ) + pen(θ) } denote a penalised
empirical risk minimiser.
body.limitation: The source uses argmin without asserting that it is nonempty.

body.excerpt:
Proof of Theorem 4.1. Combining Proposition 3.3 with Lemma 3.1 gives, for n ≥ d log d,
    E‖θ̂ − θ*‖² ≤ C σ² d / n.
The lower bound follows from Fano's inequality; see Appendix B.
